power_conversion: Convert facility-input MW to IT MW only with matching-period PUE. Do not apply PUE to capacity explicitly labeled IT MW. Aggregate PUE by IT energy, not simple site average.
capacity_time_basis: sum(cohort active AI IT MW * physical utilization * active days in period) / period days across owned, leased, colocated and purchased capacity
revenue_perimeter: Use restated Azure revenue beginning FY2026 history from the September 2 2026 exhibit; separately source AI compute attribution. Keep Intelligent Cloud, Microsoft Cloud, RPO, contract value and prepayments outside the recognized Azure AI numerator.
special: The September exhibit reports exact Azure revenue but changes the perimeter by moving GitHub/developer cloud, Security Copilot and Healthcare/Life Sciences out. Reconcile the definition before time-series comparisons. FY2025 PUE 1.17 and environmental electricity cover only owned-and-controlled full-year sites and are boundary diagnostics, not current model inputs.
failure: Missing AI-only revenue attribution, period-average active AI IT MW, physical utilization or matched full-fleet PUE; never divide Azure revenue by the 1 GW Q4 capacity addition or by PPA generation MW.
hardware_diagnostic: 96 accelerators / 0.167 MW is a Maia300 rack-envelope design ratio. Do not mix with current Azure revenue, chip TDP-only counts, off-rack loads or historical PUE.
revenue_engine: External customers buy Azure consumption or subscriptions; consumption revenue follows resource use, subscription revenue follows the service period. First-party Maia inference cost reductions need not create Azure external revenue.
replacement_risk: Separate hardware efficiency and job-packing improvements from measured fleet utilization. Test contract acceptance/minimum-fee protection, cancellation exceptions, replacement demand and collateral appraisal before inferring loss.

history.reason: Add Maia design-versus-operating boundaries and explicit revenue/payment/replacement bridge
